content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text treats Matthew 1:20 as UNDERDETERMINED because two sides gave different readings of that one verse, which is the kind of single-verse openness the rule addresses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"The phrase A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand: reading one is that two senses on one verse both stand, so they cannot make it UNDERDETERMINED; reading two is that two senses leave the one verse open, so it is UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"The judge's only stated basis for UNDERDETERMINED is that one verse was answered with two readings, which the rule forbids as a ground because both senses stand rather than leaving the verse open."}
